intro: Picture this: you open your villa door to a lush green garden with a small stream running through it, the sound of water and birdsong instead of traffic, and cool, comfortable air because you're on a mountainside at around 1,150m — Proud Phu Fah Hip & Green Resort is a small boutique eco-resort on the Mae Rim-Samoeng road in Mae Rim district, Chiang Mai province, close to Mon Cham. The draw here is villas spread out across a streamside garden, built for privacy and to blend in with nature · there are around 20 rooms/villas, some with a jacuzzi or small private pool, from about ฿2,500/night · TripAdvisor sits at around 4.2 from roughly 159 reviews.

body.html: Let's start with the big picture: Proud Phu Fah Hip & Green Resort is not a hotel in Chiang Mai city, and that's both its main selling point and the most important thing to know about it · it's a small boutique eco-resort sitting on a mountainside in Mae Rim district, on the Mae Rim-Samoeng road around the Pong Yang area, near km 18, close to the Mon Cham viewpoint that many people know · the resort itself is at around 1,150m above sea level, so the air is clearly cooler than in the city, especially in the morning and at night · the concept here is straightforward, just like the name says: "hip & green" — a resort designed to blend in with nature, with a lush green garden, a small stream running through it, and villas spread out so it feels private, more like staying in a forest on the mountain than in a single row of hotel rooms.

Who it suits · if you're a couple wanting a quiet, peaceful trip, a nature lover who wants to wake up to trees and the sound of water, or someone who's worn out and wants a place where "the hotel is the destination of the trip" rather than just somewhere to crash — this place suits you well · on the flip side, if you plan to head into the city every day, want to walk the night market, stroll Nimman, or visit temples in the old town mostly, staying up on a mountainside that's around 40 minutes or more away may not be the most convenient choice · the real reviews lean fairly consistently the same way: people who come intending to relax with nature and aren't in a rush to go anywhere usually come away very impressed, while those who expect city-hotel convenience may find the drive up and down the mountain a chore.

Location and getting there · the address is 97/5 Moo 1, Mae Rim-Samoeng road, Pong Yang, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai · from Chiang Mai city it's about a 40–60 min drive up the mountain, depending on traffic and your starting point · from Chiang Mai airport (CNX) it's roughly an hour as well · the last stretch is a winding mountain road, steep in places — a regular sedan can make it but should be driven carefully, especially in the rainy season when the road is slippery and the fog rolls in thick · if you'd rather not drive yourself, the resort offers a shuttle (for a fee, which the real reviews note is fairly high for a one-way trip), so it's worth asking for the price and booking ahead · the upside of the location is the quiet and the nature all around; the trade-off is that getting out and about isn't very convenient, so you should plan to spend most of your time at the resort, or visiting nearby spots like Mon Cham, the strawberry farms, and the botanic gardens around Mae Rim.

Rooms and decor · the resort has around 20 rooms/villas in total, split into two main zones · the Villa Zone is standalone streamside villas in the garden, spaced far enough apart to feel private, with Private Villa, Honeymoon Villa, and larger ones like the Private Pool Villa with its own small pool · the Phu Zone is a multi-storey mountain-view building with suites of around 66 sqm, some coming with a jacuzzi or small pool on the balcony, such as the Pool Suite, Mountain View Suite with Jacuzzi, and Luxury Suite · what comes up often in reviews is the room design, with glass walls looking out over the stream and trees, which makes you feel close to nature, and some villas have an outdoor shower that a lot of people love · one thing reviews do flag is upkeep in places, which is starting to show its age — some rooms may look older than in the photos, so go in knowing this place sells natural charm and atmosphere more than the spotless newness of a brand-new hotel.

"Woke up in the morning, opened the door to a green garden with a stream running past the villa, the sound of water and birds instead of traffic — it really felt like staying in a forest. Hard to believe it's this close to Chiang Mai city."

Facilities, pool, and spa · the heart of this place is the streamside garden and the natural surroundings · there's an outdoor swimming pool for guests, not very big but a good fit for the garden setting, better for a relaxing soak than for swimming laps · for rooms listed with a private pool or jacuzzi, you get your own soaking space on the balcony or in the villa, which is what a lot of couples choose · on the wellness side, the resort offers Thai massage and relaxing treatments, perfect for a massage after walking around Mon Cham or wandering the garden · there are also streamside seating areas, several garden corners, and according to the resort, a Thai cooking class and a small playground too · the real reviews speak very positively about how shady the garden is and how private the villas feel — many say just strolling around the resort and sitting listening to the water is worth the trip on its own.

Food and bar · the resort restaurant is open from morning to evening, serving mainly Thai food with an à la carte menu · what comes up repeatedly in reviews is breakfast, which comes in several styles — American, Chinese, and vegetarian — and the restaurant staff get special praise for how friendly they are · many reviews note that the ingredients are fresh, the food is freshly made, and the menu can be adjusted for dietary restrictions · because the resort is on a remote mountainside, there aren't many dining options outside it — although there are some cafés and restaurants with good views around Mon Cham, if you want every meal without having to drive far, eating at the resort is the main option, so budget for this in your planning · the experience of sitting and eating by the garden in the cool air is another thing reviews mention favourably.

Service · this is where Proud Phu Fah gets the most consistent praise from the real reviews · being a small resort of around 20 rooms, the staff can look after guests thoroughly in a way large hotels find hard to match · many reviews use words like smiling, friendly, and willing to help, with some saying the team handled things wonderfully even in tricky situations · plenty of people say the warmth of the staff is what made their stay memorable and the reason they'd come back · for anyone worried about the trip up and down the mountain, the team can help arrange transport and suggest nearby spots to visit.

Garden, stream, and the natural setting · what sets this place apart from typical mountain resorts is the way it's laid out to blend in with the green space and the natural stream · the garden is planted with a variety of tropical species, shady in a semi-forest way, with a small stream running through the middle of the resort so each villa gets a different view and a different sound of water · many of the real reviews describe feeling like they're staying in the middle of a forest, hearing birds and water all day, and the privacy that comes from the villas being spaced apart · for anyone who likes taking photos, the garden corners, the stream, and the room's glass walls are a backdrop a lot of people enjoy shooting · this kind of atmosphere fits a slower pace, good for sitting with a book, sipping coffee, or wandering to soak up a quiet you rarely find in the city.

Nearby spots that pair well with a stay · because the resort is on a mountainside around Pong Yang, planning to visit nearby spots in a single day makes more sense than heading down into the city every day · the most popular spot closest by is Mon Cham, with flower farms, seasonal strawberry farms, and a sea-of-fog viewpoint, just a short drive away · nearby there are also strawberry and orange farms only a few kilometres off · on the nature-activity side, Mae Sa Elephant Camp and a zipline/Jungle Coaster spot are not far · and on the way down towards Mae Rim there's Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, which you can walk around all day · a trip set up as "wake up easy at the resort in the morning, head out to Mon Cham or a mountain café late morning, come back in the afternoon to soak and relax in the villa" is the most natural fit for a location like this — no tiring drives up and down the mountain multiple times.

Voices from the real reviews — the good and the not-so-good · on the praise side, most people credit the natural atmosphere that feels like staying in a forest, the shady streamside green garden, the privacy of the villas, the cool comfortable mountain air, the friendly and attentive staff, and the breakfast that comes in several styles · there are international reviews saying it's a good place to come and unwind from stress and that it's worth the money · on the criticism side, what comes up often is the long trip up the mountain and the winding road, which make getting into the city inconvenient, and the resort shuttle fee that's fairly high · some reviews mention upkeep in places starting to show its age, and there's a review disappointed about getting a room that didn't match expectations (for example, getting a room in a building instead of a standalone villa) · the overall numbers back up this picture — TripAdvisor gives it around 4.2 from roughly 159 reviews, ranking it among the top hotels in the Mae Rim area · and Trip.com has several dozen main reviews in a similar tone.

Price comparison and value · the starting price for a standard room/villa is around ฿2,500–3,500/night during promotions or the off-season, and can climb to roughly ฿6,000–9,000+ for a suite with a jacuzzi or a villa with a private pool during peak periods · this price sits at a more accessible level than many ryokan or luxury mountain resorts around Mae Rim, making it a good choice for anyone who wants the natural streamside atmosphere without paying five-star rates · the value is highest when you genuinely come to relax at the resort, spend time with the garden and the stream, soak in a room with a private pool/jacuzzi, and visit nearby spots like Mon Cham · but if the plan is to use this place purely as a bed and head into the city every day, the room rate plus the time and cost of driving up and down the mountain will make it feel less worthwhile than it should, and you should compare it against a city stay that's easier to get around from.

Things to know before booking · one, the trip — allow at least 40 minutes to an hour to get up the mountain; if you're not driving yourself, ask about the resort shuttle fee in advance because it may be higher than you think, and if you are driving, check your car and fuel before heading up · two, the air on the mountain is cooler than in the city, especially morning and night in winter, so bring warm clothes · three, if you want a standalone streamside villa or a room with a private pool/jacuzzi, you need to pick a clearly specified room type and confirm with the resort first — don't assume every room is a standalone villa · four, this place sells natural charm and atmosphere, not spotless newness, so make some allowance for signs of age in places · five, budget for food at the resort because options outside are limited · six, in the rainy season the fog rolls in thick and the road gets slippery, but the misty atmosphere and the lush green garden are a charm of their own for some people.

The verdict · Proud Phu Fah Hip & Green Resort is a boutique eco-resort that pulls off the "streamside villas in a green garden on a mountainside" concept in a lovely, accessible way at a price that isn't too high · its strengths are the natural atmosphere that feels like staying in a forest, the privacy of the villas, the shady garden and stream, the cool mountain air near Mon Cham, the friendly staff, and the breakfast that comes in several styles · the trade-offs you have to accept are the location far from the city, a trip up the mountain that takes planning and a high shuttle fee, few dining options outside the resort, and upkeep in places starting to show its age · if you're after a slower-paced getaway, want to wake up to trees and the sound of water, and want the resort to be the main destination of your trip, this place gives a worthwhile experience at an accessible price · but if the heart of your trip is exploring the city every day, choosing a city stay that's easier to get around from is probably a better fit for you.

honestSummary: Proud Phu Fah Hip & Green Resort is a good stay for anyone who wants streamside villas in a green garden on a Mae Rim mountainside at an accessible price — a natural atmosphere that feels like staying in a forest, privacy, cool air, and friendly staff · but you have to accept that the location is far from the city, the trip up the mountain and the shuttle fee need budgeting for, and upkeep in places is starting to show its age.

tips.title: Allow time for the climb · check the shuttle fee first
tips.body: From Chiang Mai city it's around 40–60 min up a winding road; if you're not driving yourself, ask the resort shuttle fee in advance as it may be high.

tips.title: Choose a standalone streamside villa
tips.body: If you want full privacy, pick a room in the streamside Villa Zone, not a room in the Phu zone building — confirm the room type before booking.

tips.body: The air on the mountain is cooler than in the city, especially morning and night in winter, so pack something warm.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Proud Phu Fah Hip & Green Resort Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Proud Phu Fah · how do you get there from Chiang Mai city?
faq.a: Proud Phu Fah Hip & Green Resort is located at 97/5 Moo 1, Mae Rim-Samoeng road km 18, Pong Yang, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, on a mountainside at around 1,150m, near Mon Cham · from Chiang Mai city and CNX airport it's about a 40–60 min drive up the mountain · the last stretch is a winding mountain road, so if you're not driving yourself you can ask about the resort shuttle (for a fee — check the price first).

faq.q: What's the starting price at Proud Phu Fah · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,500/night for a standard villa during promotions or the off-season · suites with a jacuzzi are around ฿4,500 and up, and the Private Pool Villa with a private pool is around ฿8,500+ · there's a streamside Villa Zone (Private Villa, Honeymoon Villa) and a Phu zone with mountain-view suites · prices depend on the period and package, so always compare across several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Proud Phu Fah best suited to?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, nature lovers, or anyone who wants a slower-paced getaway in a green streamside garden · the focus is on quiet, privacy, and making the resort the destination of the trip · it's not ideal for people who want to explore the city every day, because the location is on a mountainside around 40–60 min from the city.

faq.q: Is there a swimming pool or rooms with a private pool here?
faq.a: Yes · the resort has a shared outdoor swimming pool for guests, and some room/villa types come with a jacuzzi or small private pool, such as the Pool Suite, Mountain View Suite with Jacuzzi, and Private Pool Villa · if you want a pool or jacuzzi in your room, you need to pick a clearly specified room type and confirm with the resort before booking.

faq.q: Is there anything special to prepare for a stay here?
faq.a: Bring warm clothes because the air on the mountain is cooler than in the city, especially morning and night in winter · allow time and budget for the trip up and down the mountain · budget for food at the resort because there are few options outside · and go in knowing this place sells natural charm, not the spotless newness of a brand-new hotel.

Proud Phu Fah can be booked through the main platforms — Booking.com and Trip.com — as well as the official website proudphufah.com · for Agoda you can search the hotel name in the system to check prices and availability · we recommend comparing prices across several platforms and choosing Free Cancellation if your plans aren't yet certain.
